items.title: Fourteen More Gateways: Real or Nominal, Cause or Result, Which Feeling, Which Suffering

items.zh: 是十二支緣起，幾支是實有？謂九。幾支非實有？謂餘。幾一事為自性？謂五。幾非一事為自性？謂餘。幾是所知障因？謂一。幾能生苦？謂五。幾苦胎藏？謂五。幾唯是苦？謂二。
items.en: Of these twelve links, how many genuinely exist in their own right? Nine. How many do not, existing only as composite labels? The rest — becoming, birth, and old-age-and-death. How many consist of a single thing? Five — ignorance, consciousness, contact, feeling, and craving. How many consist of more than one thing combined? The rest. How many are the specific cause of the obstruction to omniscience? One — ignorance. How many actually generate suffering? Five — ignorance, formations, craving, grasping, and becoming. How many are suffering still hidden in embryo, as unripened seed? Five — consciousness through feeling. How many are simply suffering itself, already manifest? Two — birth and old-age-and-death.

items.zh: 幾說為因分？謂前六，無明乃至觸，及愛、取、有三，說為因分。幾說為果分？謂後二說為果分。幾說為雜因果分？謂所餘支說為雜分。所以者何？有二種受名為雜分。一、謂後法以觸為緣因受；二、謂現法與愛為緣果受。此二雜說為觸緣受。復次，幾支能生愛非愛境界果？幾支能生自體果？謂前六支能生前果，後三支能生後果，一支俱生二果。
items.en: How many count as the cause-portion? Nine — ignorance through contact, together with craving, grasping, and becoming. How many count as the result-portion? Two — birth and old-age-and-death. How many count as a mixed cause-and-result portion? The one remaining link, feeling — which is, as a seed, the cause conditioning a future life, and, as present experience, the result that serves as the condition for craving. Further: how many links generate a desirable or undesirable environmental result? How many generate the very embodiment itself? The first six links generate the former result, the last three generate the latter, and the one remaining link generates both at once.

items.zh: 復次，幾支樂受俱行？謂除二，所餘支。幾支苦受俱行？謂即彼及所除中一。幾支不苦不樂受俱行？謂如樂受道理應知。幾支不與受俱行？謂所除中一。復次，幾支壞苦攝？謂樂受俱行支及非受俱行支一分。幾支苦苦攝？謂苦受俱行支及非受俱行支一分。
items.en: Further: how many links occur together with pleasant feeling? All but two — feeling itself, and old-age-and-death. How many occur together with painful feeling? Those same ten, together with old-age-and-death — eleven in all. How many occur together with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling? The same as for pleasant feeling. How many never occur together with feeling at all? The one remaining — feeling itself. Further: how many links belong to the suffering of change? The links occurring with pleasant feeling, together with a portion of feeling itself. How many belong to the suffering of pain? The links occurring with painful feeling, together with a further portion of feeling itself.

items.title: Five More Gateways: Formations' Suffering, What Meditation Removes, and Which Realm Each Link Belongs To

items.zh: 幾支行苦攝？謂所有壞苦、苦苦支，亦是行苦支。或有行苦所攝，非餘二苦。謂不苦不樂受俱行支及非受俱行支一分。問：於一切生處及三摩鉢底中，皆有一切支現行可得耶？答：不可得。謂無想天中，及滅盡定、無想定中，有色支可得，非無色支。若生無色界，無色支可得，非有色支。問：
items.en: How many links belong to the suffering of formations? Every link belonging to the suffering of change or the suffering of pain also belongs to the suffering of formations; and there is, further, a portion belonging to the suffering of formations alone, apart from those other two kinds of suffering — the links occurring with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, together with a further portion of feeling itself. Are all twelve links present, manifest, in every place of birth and every meditative attainment? Answer: They are not. In the non-perception heaven, in cessation attainment, and in the attainment without perception, only the physical links are present, not the formless ones. Reborn in the formless realm, only the formless links are present, not the physical ones.

items.zh: 頗有依支得離支耶？答：有。謂依上地支離下地支。此但一分，非全；唯暫時，非究竟。問：幾支染污，幾支不染污？答：三染。餘通二種，若不染污，善及無覆無記別故，分為二種應知。問：幾支欲界繫？答：一切支，和合等起故。
items.en: Is there a case where resting on one link, another link can be left behind? Answer: There is — resting on a higher meditative level's formations, a lower level's formations can be left behind. But this applies to only a portion, formations alone, never the whole chain; and only temporarily, while absorbed in that meditative state, never as a final, permanent removal. How many links are purely defiled, and how many are not? Answer: Three are purely defiled; the rest can be either. When not defiled, they divide further into wholesome and morally neutral. How many links belong to the desire realm? Answer: All twelve, since they arise there together as a single unified whole.

items.zh: 問：幾支色界繫？答：一切一分。問：云何應知彼有老耶？答：彼諸行有朽壞腐敗性故。如色界繫，當知無色界繫亦爾。問：
items.en: Question: How many links belong to the form realm? Answer: All of them, in part. Question: How should it be understood that there is ageing there? Answer: Because the formations there are subject to decay and decline. As with the form realm, so likewise should the formless realm be understood. Question:

items.title: The Final Gateways: Training-Level, and How Much Each Noble Fruit Actually Cuts — 緣起分別緣 Closes Entirely

items.zh: 幾支是學？答：無。問：幾支是無學？答：亦無。問：幾支是非學非無學？答：一切。問：所有善有漏支，彼何故非學耶？答：墮流轉故。若學所有善有漏法，彼與流轉相違故，及用明為緣故，非支。問：
items.en: How many links belong to one still in training? None. How many belong to one beyond training? None, either. How many belong to neither — an ordinary being? All twelve. Why is even an ordinary being's wholesome, contaminated conduct not counted as belonging to a trainee? Because it still falls within transmigration. A trainee's own wholesome, contaminated conduct runs contrary to transmigration, and is conditioned by genuine insight rather than ignorance — so it, too, does not belong among the twelve links at all.

items.zh: 預流果當言幾支已斷耶？答：一切一分，無全斷者。如預流果，如是一來果亦爾。問：不還果當言幾支已斷耶？答：欲界一切，色無色界不定。問：阿羅漢當言幾支已斷耶？答：三界一切。
items.en: Of a stream-enterer, how many links should be said to be already severed? A portion of every link, but none entirely. Just as with a stream-enterer, so too with a once-returner. Of a non-returner, how many links should be said to be already severed? All belonging to the desire realm; those of the form and formless realms remain undetermined. Of an arhat, how many links should be said to be already severed? All, throughout all three realms, without exception.

items.title: The Ninth and Final Topic: Six Ways the Sūtras Themselves Teach Dependent Origination

items.zh: 復次，於彼彼經中，由幾種言說道理說緣起耶？謂略說由六種言說道理：一、由順次第說，二、由逆次第說，三、由一分支說，四、由具分支說，五、由黑品說，六、由白品說。
items.en: Further, across the various sūtras, by how many kinds of exposition is dependent origination taught? Briefly, by six. First, taught in forward sequence. Second, taught in reverse sequence. Third, taught through a single link. Fourth, taught through every link in full. Fifth, taught as the darkened portion, tracing how suffering accumulates. Sixth, taught as the bright portion, tracing how it is dismantled.
Question: As the World-Honoured One said, dependent arising is very deep;

items.zh: 此甚深義云何應知？答：由十種相，應知緣起甚深義。謂依無常義、苦義、空義、無我義說。
items.en: "Because what does old-age-and-death exist? What is old-age-and-death's condition?" Having reflected thus, direct realisation arose: because birth exists, old-age-and-death exists; birth is old-age-and-death's condition. ... "It is at consciousness that my mind should turn back." He further reflected: "Absent what does this old age, sickness, and death not exist? What ceasing causes old age, sickness, and death to cease?" Reflecting rightly, direct, unbroken realisation arose: absent birth, there is no old age, sickness, or death; birth ceasing, old age, sickness, and death cease — down to: ignorance ceasing, formations cease; formations ceasing, consciousness ceases ... birth ceasing, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, grief, distress, and suffering cease — and thus this whole great mass of suffering ceases.

items.title: Ten Aspects of Profound Meaning: Not Self-Made, Not Other-Made, Not Both, Not Uncaused

items.zh: 依無常義者，謂從自種子生，亦待他緣。又從他緣生，亦待自種子。又從自種子及從他緣生，而種及緣於此生事無作、無用，亦無運轉。又復此二因性功能非不是有。又諸有支雖無始來其相成就，然剎那剎那新新相轉。又緣起支雖剎那速滅，然似停住運動相現。
items.en: As for the meaning of impermanence: a link arises from its own seed, yet also depends on other conditions — so it is not self-made. It arises from other conditions, yet also depends on its own seed — so it is not other-made. It arises from both its own seed and other conditions together, yet neither the seed nor the conditions perform any real action, exert any real function, or undergo any real operation in producing it — so it is not made by both together. And yet the causal capacity of these two is not simply absent — so it is not uncaused. Further, though every link's own character has been established since beginningless time, each instant it turns anew, ever fresh. And further, though a link perishes with instantaneous speed, it appears as though it were a stationary thing in motion.

items.zh: 依苦義者，謂緣起支一味苦相，而似三種相現。依空義者，謂緣起支雖離有情、作者、受者，然似不離顯現而說。依無我義者，謂緣起支雖不自在，實無有我相，然似我相顯現，依勝義諦，諸法自性雖不可說，而言諸法自性可說。問：
items.en: As for the meaning of suffering: every link carries one single taste of suffering, yet appears as though it presented three different tastes. As for the meaning of emptiness: every link is free of any true being, agent, or experiencer, and yet appears as though it were not free of them. As for the meaning of selflessness: every link, though never truly under its own mastery and genuinely without any self-nature, still appears as though a self-nature were present. And resting on ultimate truth, though the true nature of things cannot actually be spoken, it is still spoken of as though it could be.

blocks.text: Today the treatise runs the twelve links through a long series of classifications, each a question with a short answer: how many are real, how many are causes, which feelings and which sufferings they involve, which belong to which realm and to which stage of the path. It then begins the ninth and last heading, how the sūtras teach dependent origination, and its ten profound meanings.

"How many genuinely exist in their own right? Nine. The rest do not." Venerable Miào Jìng's example of a nominal link: becoming. "Apart from formations there's no separate 'becoming'"; it is the name for karmic seeds once moistened. Birth and old age and death are likewise names for phases of the aggregates.

"How many are suffering still in the womb? Five." Master Cháng Bǎi: "womb" here means the seed: consciousness through feeling, present as seeds before they ripen. All the links of the suffering of pain and of change also belong to the **suffering of formations**. Venerable Miào Jìng: "Only the noble can feel the suffering of formations as suffering; we ordinary beings don't."

One link is the cause of the **cognitive obstruction** (所知障): ignorance. Master Cháng Bǎi: bodhisattvas must cut it too, to benefit beings fully and attain Buddhahood. This is the Mahāyāna addition to the arhat's path.

In the heaven of no perception and the attainment of cessation, "only physical links" are present. Venerable Miào Jìng adds a Yogācāra caveat: this speaks of the six consciousnesses; counting the ālayavijñāna, mental links are still present. This is one of the classic arguments for the ālayavijñāna (Day 4: something must hold the body when the mind stops).

subs.head: Trainees, adepts, and the four fruits

blocks.text: "How many links belong to one in training? None. Beyond training? None. To neither? All twelve." The links are the process of saṃsāra; what trainees and adepts practise is not one of them. Venerable Miào Jìng: an ordinary person's good deeds are still links "when self-grasping stirs", because without cutting self-view they keep one in the round.

What does each noble fruit cut? A stream-enterer has cut "a portion of every link, but none entirely"; so too a once-returner. A non-returner has cut all links of the desire realm. An arhat has cut all, in all three realms. Venerable Miào Jìng: three fruits are needed for the desire realm because, without strong concentration, its afflictions are hard to cut.

subs.head: Six ways of teaching; ten profound meanings

blocks.text: The sūtras teach dependent origination in six ways: forward, reverse, through one link, through all, in its dark portion (saṃsāra), and in its bright portion (its ending). Venerable Miào Jìng: both the turning and the stopping of the wheel can be taught forwards or backwards.

Its ten profound meanings include that the links are "not self-made, not other-made, not both, not uncaused". Venerable Miào Jìng: "self" is the seed, the causal condition; "other" is the remaining conditions. Neither alone produces anything. This is the same fourfold denial Nāgārjuna uses, read in Yogācāra terms.

quiz.q: How many links genuinely exist? Which does Venerable Miào Jìng use to show a nominal one?
options: nine are real, three nominal — e.g. becoming: apart from formations there's no separate "becoming"
quiz.why: "How many genuinely exist in their own right? Nine. How many do not …? The rest." Venerable Miào Jìng: "Apart from formations there's no 'becoming' to be found, so becoming is nominal" — it's formations moistened by craving and grasping. Master Cháng Bǎi: the unreal are composites, conventionally designated.

quiz.q: "How many are suffering still in the womb? Five." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "in the womb"?
options: it means the cause, the seed — suffering still hidden as in a womb, in seed form
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "'Womb' really means the cause — the seed — of suffering: suffering still hidden in the womb, in seed form." These five are consciousness through feeling; the two that are simply suffering are birth and old-age-and-death.

quiz.q: All links of the suffering of change and of pain also belong to the suffering of formations. What's special about it, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: only the noble can perceive it; ordinary beings don't feel it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Only the noble can feel the suffering of formations as suffering; we ordinary beings don't — it feels like nothing to us." Master Cháng Bǎi: all twelve links, indeed all contaminated things, belong to the suffering of formations.

quiz.q: How many links belong to trainees, adepts, and neither?
options: trainees none, adepts none, neither — all twelve
quiz.why: "How many links belong to one still in training? None. How many belong to one beyond training? None, either. How many belong to neither …? All twelve." A trainee's good conduct "runs contrary to transmigration, and is conditioned by genuine insight." Master Cháng Bǎi: diligent practitioners' deeds aren't ignorance-conditioned formations.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how many links has a stream-enterer severed?
options: a portion of every link, none entirely
quiz.why: "A portion of every link, but none entirely. Just as with a stream-enterer, so too with a once-returner." Master Cháng Bǎi: stream-entry cuts the links leading to the lower realms, leaving seven rebirths — fourteen lives among humans and gods.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how many links have the non-returner and the arhat severed?
options: non-returner: all of the desire realm, the higher realms undetermined; arhat: all in all three realms
quiz.why: "Of a non-returner … All belonging to the desire realm; those of the form and formless realms remain undetermined. Of an arhat … All, throughout all three realms." Master Cháng Bǎi: in the highest pure abode, the noble path manifests and the fourth fruit is attained.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, by how many kinds of exposition do the sūtras teach dependent origination?
options: six: forward, reverse, a single link, every link, the dark portion, the bright portion
quiz.why: "First, taught in forward sequence. Second, taught in reverse sequence. Third, taught through a single link. Fourth, taught through every link in full. Fifth, taught as the darkened portion … Sixth, taught as the bright portion." Venerable Miào Jìng: all beings transmigrating from start to end is the full-link exposition.
